note: Rustic DNR state-forest campground beside the public landing (dock and boat access) at the south end of Greer Lake, about 20 miles northeast of Brainerd, with the Bass Lake Nature Trail loops starting at the campground. Off-highway vehicle riders may ride in and out of the campground directly. Managed by Cuyuna Country State Recreation Area. --Claude
summary: DNR facility cmp00010 read: 31 primitive drive-in sites, vault toilets, well water, garbage, dock/landing; $17 tax-included, same-day online payment (fee note corrected). Lakeview -> not waterfront proposed (loop 55-65 m back under forest, no view shown). OHV side flagged. Phone and website fixes.
flags: WATERFRONT lakeview -> not waterfront proposed (defaults down; no --AWH value). The stored evidence ('loop sites set ~40m back behind treed shore fringe ... nearest sites overlook lake') is not borne out on imagery: the DNR facility map and Esri z18/z19 frames put the campground loops in mixed pine and hardwood forest south of the lake's south bay; the nearest loop road (around 46.6328,-94.0393) is about 55-65 m from the shore, behind a continuous band of conifers along the bank. The leaf-on NAIP frame shows unbroken canopy between every loop and the water; only the public landing (gravel ramp lot at about 46.6330,-94.0411) reaches the shore, and it is day use. No DNR photo or site map shows a site with a lake view, and sites are not numbered on any official map. With no view confirmed, the value goes down to not waterfront; reviewer may keep lakeview if a site photo shows the lake through the trees.

OHV side (flag, no drop): DNR 'This campground allows off-highway vehicle riders to enter and exit the campground directly.' A general state-forest campground (lake landing, dock, nature trail) with OHV access, not an OHV staging camp. Kept in the note.
SITES max_rig_ft 35 (derived from old note prose) is not stated anywhere on the current DNR pages or facility map; left in place, reviewer may clear it.
SEASON 05-01..11-30 'Approximate: Open May to November' (derived from note prose) is not stated by the DNR; left in place as unverified, reviewer may clear it.

FEES note corrected: the stored note said 'first come, first served, paid at the campground'; the DNR fee page says 'DNR does not accept self-payment envelopes on site' and 'Onsite staff cannot accept camping fee payments'; payment is online on the arrival date or at a state park ranger station. Rate $17 unchanged.
PHONE missing: DNR facility record names the manager as Cuyuna Country State Recreation Area, 218-772-3690. Suggest 218-772-3690.

Pin 46.63080,-94.04020 sits on the campground entrance road near the forest-road junction, about 170 m SSW of the DNR facility point 46.632332,-94.039842 and about 150 m from the loops' centre (about 46.6322,-94.0398); under 250 m, no move required. No DNR alerts for this forest.

Note cleaned: dropped '31 drive-in primitive sites (no hookups)', 'vault toilets, drinking water', 'sites fit rigs to ~35 ft' and 'Open ~May-Nov' (fields hold them); added the landing, the OHV access and the managing park.
